catalogue: cloud cost market watch — standing optimisation opportunities
note: Curated by the team from published vendor pricing pages and public FinOps practice. Reduction bands are the PUBLISHED / industry-typical ranges for each move, not measurements taken on this estate; applies_to_share is the team's stated assumption about how much of a service's spend the move can touch. Every figure the operator sees is arithmetic over these bands and the estate's own run rate — nothing here is model-generated.

opportunities.headline: Commitment discount on steady-state compute
opportunities.rationale: The share of the estate that runs around the clock is paying on-demand rates. A one-year, no-upfront commitment (savings plan / reserved capacity) is the cheapest lever with no architectural change.
opportunities.watch_out: Commitment is a financial lock-in: size it to the trough of the last quarter, never to the peak.
opportunities.source: AWS Savings Plans & Azure Reservations published pricing guidance

opportunities.headline: ARM-based instance families for stateless workloads
opportunities.rationale: ARM families (Graviton, Cobalt, Axion) are published at materially better price-performance than comparable x86 for stateless services that rebuild cleanly on another architecture.
opportunities.watch_out: Needs a multi-arch build and a soak test; native dependencies are where migrations stall.
opportunities.source: Vendor price-performance pages for ARM server families

opportunities.headline: Non-production shutdown outside working hours
opportunities.rationale: A weekday 09:00-19:00 schedule leaves roughly two thirds of the week's hours unused. Dev, test and staging rarely need to survive the night.
opportunities.watch_out: Nightly pipelines and scheduled jobs must be excluded before the first shutdown window.
opportunities.source: Standard FinOps scheduling practice (168h week vs 50h working window)

opportunities.headline: Lifecycle tiering for cold object storage
opportunities.rationale: Objects untouched past the access window cost the same as hot data until a lifecycle rule moves them. Infrequent-access and archive tiers are published well below standard storage.
opportunities.watch_out: Retrieval fees and minimum storage durations make archive tiers expensive for data that is actually read.
opportunities.source: Object storage tier pricing tables (standard vs infrequent-access vs archive)

opportunities.headline: Next-generation block storage volumes
opportunities.rationale: Current-generation block volumes are published below the previous generation per GB while decoupling IOPS from capacity, so provisioned throughput stops being bought as unused disk.
opportunities.watch_out: Baseline throughput differs between generations — check IOPS-hungry volumes before a blanket migration.
opportunities.source: Block storage per-GB pricing, current vs previous generation

opportunities.headline: Spot / pre-emptible capacity for interruptible batch
opportunities.rationale: Spare-capacity pricing is published far below on-demand. Batch, CI and rendering tolerate interruption and are the natural first movers.
opportunities.watch_out: Only for work that can be killed and retried; never for the request path or stateful singletons.

opportunities.headline: Idle and orphaned resource sweep
opportunities.rationale: Unattached volumes, idle load balancers, forgotten snapshots and stopped instances still holding storage are pure waste — the cheapest saving in any estate because nothing is using them.
opportunities.watch_out: Confirm ownership before deleting; a quiet volume can still be somebody's disaster-recovery copy.
opportunities.source: Public FinOps waste surveys (idle and unattached resources)

opportunities.headline: Egress and cross-zone traffic routing
opportunities.rationale: Managed NAT and cross-zone chatter are billed per GB. Private endpoints, zone-aware placement and a CDN in front of repeat traffic remove whole categories of transfer charges.
opportunities.watch_out: Zone-aware placement trades some resilience headroom — review with the availability target in hand.
opportunities.source: Data transfer and NAT gateway per-GB pricing

opportunities.headline: Observability retention tiering
opportunities.rationale: Log and metric retention is usually set once and never revisited. Hot retention for the debugging window plus cold archive for compliance costs a fraction of hot-everything.
opportunities.watch_out: Compliance and incident-forensics windows set the floor — legal before finance on this one.
opportunities.source: Log ingestion and retention pricing tiers
